title: Bucket-histogram KV allocator and batch-aligned packing playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We propose a new allocation strategy for the KV cache ("bucket-histogram allocator") paired with a batch-aligned packing policy and a low-latency background relocation mechanism (vapor sweep). The goal is to reduce fragmentation caused by variable-lived token slots and continuous batching patterns, lower OOM/pressure events on GPUs, and improve steady-state throughput and tail latency for online workloads.

Design goals and constraints:
- Minimize per-GPU fragmentation without introducing high tail-latency or blocking operations in the hot-path.
- Support continuous batching: allocator decisions should be aware of observed batch size distributions and prefix reuse patterns.
- Operate within strict GPU memory/time budgets: relocation work must be opportunistic and bounded by per-node throttles.
- Keep interop simple with existing indirection layer: support a light-weight forwarding entry for moved slots, tolerating a small lookup-cost for cold-moved tokens.

Core ideas:
1) Bucketed time-decayed residency histograms:
   - Maintain a small per-GPU histogram of token residency durations split into buckets (e.g., <1s, 1-5s, 5-30s, 30s-5m, >5m). Use recent requests with exponential decay to keep the histogram responsive.
   - When allocating a new KV entry, pick a bucket whose size/capacity fits the request and whose expected lifetime statistically matches the prefix's recent history (derived from prefix access telemetry). This reduces long-lived entries being placed into small fragmented slots.

2) Batch-aligned packing policy:
   - Observe batch size distribution at runtime (sliding window). Use the distribution to prefer contiguous allocations sized to common batch footprints (e.g., allocate blocks in units approximating the 50th/90th percentiles of batch slot needs).
   - For streaming/low-latency requests where batches are small but frequent, prefer smaller granular buckets to reduce internal waste. For high-throughput batched workloads, skew allocation to larger contiguous blocks to improve packing efficiency and reduce cross-batch fragmentation.

3) Vapor sweep: non-blocking micro-relocation during low-util windows:
   - Background relocations are scheduled only when GPU utilization and request queue depth are below configured SLO thresholds. Relocations move cold buckets into consolidated contiguous regions to create larger free spans for hot allocations.
   - Use an indirection table for moved slots. Indirection entries are compact and cached; lookups pay a small penalty for relocated entries but avoid stop-the-world compactions.

4) Admission and eviction integration:
   - Admission policy uses bucket-fit + prefix-affinity: prefer reusing a prefix's previous bucket when possible.
   - Eviction favors the highest-fragmentation-prone buckets and uses age-weighted heuristics combined with tokengain estimates to avoid evicting entries that would cause re-population churn.

Telemetry and metrics (must be implemented before rollout):
- Per-bucket occupancy and fragmentation ratio (free bytes in bucket / total bucket capacity) sampled per-GPU.
- Relocation work rate and average relocation latency; count of requests that hit indirection entries.
- Fragmentation impact metric: average contiguous free-span size distribution and 95th percentile.
- OOM/pressure frequency and time-to-recover.
- End-to-end P95/P99 token generation latency and throughput under representative workloads.

Experiment plan:
1) Simulation harness: replay production traces (last 7 days) in the offline simulator to compare current allocator vs bucket-histogram with batching-aware packing. Key signals: fragmentation delta, peak memory pressure, and throughput.
2) Canary on dedicated nodes: enable allocator on a small fleet of dedicated instances for non-critical tenants. Monitor fragmentation, indirection hit-rate, latency regressions.
3) Progressive rollout with automated rollback criteria: rollback if P99 latency increases by >10% for 10m or OOM events increase by >2x.

Trade-offs and failure modes:
- Indirection overhead: small extra lookup cost for relocated slots; mitigated by caching indirections and limiting relocation frequency.
- Complexity in allocator heuristics: tuning required to avoid oscillation between bucket sizes for mixed workloads.
- Relocation during misdetected "low-util" windows could impact latency; we bound relocation by util/SLO checks and rate-limits.

Acceptance criteria:
- Offline simulations show >=40% reduction in fragmentation metric for conversational workloads with mixed prefix lengths, and <=3% change in mean latency.
- Canary nodes show no regression in P99 beyond the rollback threshold and indirection hit-rate <5% after warm-up period.
- No increase in OOM incident count during a 2-week pilot.

Rollout steps and tasks:
- Instrumentation: add per-bucket and span telemetry endpoints and Grafana dashboards (ENG-616000).
- Simulator: extend offline simulator to consume histograms and batching profiles (ENG-616001).
- Runtime changes: allocator core, batch-observer, relocation controller, indirection table, admission/eviction hooks. Keep changes behind feature flag.
- Safety: canary policy, automated monitors, and rollback playbook.

comments: 2026-03-11 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial design posted. Focused on matching life-expectancy to allocation granularity and reducing cross-batch fragmentation. Asked for ops/telemetry input.

2026-03-12 - Priya Menon (SRE): Telemetry endpoints look good; recommend adding a relocation-rate gate tied to node-level GPU util and request queue depth. Suggested thresholds and alerting rules. See SRE notes in design doc.

2026-03-12 - Mateo Alvarez: Prototype allocator loop implemented in sandbox runtime branch. Early local runs show contiguous free-span median increased by ~28% on a conversational trace. Pushing simulator PR for full trace runs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1428

2026-03-13 - Ben Carter (ML Infra): Concern about indirection cache pressure. Proposed LRU-style indirection caching with spillback to host memory if needed. We'll measure indirection hit-rate in canary.

2026-03-14 - Aisha Kapoor: Updated acceptance criteria after simulation results. Added explicit rollback thresholds and canary gating. Next: wire up Grafana dashboard and prepare ENG-616000/ENG-616001 tasks.
2026-03-14 - QA (Rina Zhou): Test plan notes: create synthetic workloads that alternate hot prefix storms and long-tail cold prefixes to validate relocation safety and bucket-responsiveness.
